page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.16xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the High Clock Speed family. It is built on the KVM hypervisor and powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 3.1 GHz. The instance delivers 64 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is provisioned at 128.0 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. No dedicated local storage is bundled with this instance type, requiring workloads to rely entirely on external network-attached volumes, while host networking maintains a baseline bandwidth of 20 Gbps.

Hardware vector instruction support includes AVX, AVX-512 Foundation (avx512f), and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside standard cryptographic acceleration via AES. In empirical benchmark runs, the processor demonstrates strong results in extended CPU instructions, scoring 57,136.8 in PassMark extended tests. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached a top-tier 209.21 GB/sec, matching strong multi-threaded compression metrics such as 269.5 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. PassMark database operations also tested in the upper quartile at 22,550.06 operations. However, generative LLM text generation tested in the lower quartile, reflecting the absence of dedicated accelerators for matrix-intensive autoregressive token generation.

Without integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage arrays, ecs.hfc6.16xlarge optimizes cost efficiency specifically around parallel CPU-bound compute tasks and high memory-bandwidth streaming. The 1:2 memory ratio makes it cost-inefficient for RAM-heavy in-memory caching platforms, but highly aligned with dense parallel computation. Best-fit deployments include multi-threaded batch data processing, Clang-based software build clusters, database engines requiring high transactional CPU capacity, and parallel mathematical simulations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc6.16xlarge is a high-clock-speed, compute-optimized instance running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 3.1 GHz, it provides 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores and 128.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio. It includes no bundled local disks and features a 20 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results indicate strong uncached memory read throughput at 209.21 GB/sec, high multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 269.5 GB/sec, and strong PassMark database throughput. Conversely, token generation for large language models remains weak without discrete GPU acceleration. The instance offers resource efficiency for compute-intensive batch processing, enterprise compilation pipelines, static web delivery clusters, and high-frequency relational database workloads where local disk storage is decoupled.
